Jonas to attach kernel-level logs and tail-latency graphs by 2027-01-13

Jonas Reed - provide kernel-level logs, p99 tail-latency graphs, and model variant mapping - due 2027-01-13

summary: Follow-up on the Jan 8 outage affecting inference latency spikes. Discussed root cause (batching interaction + kernel fallback under spike), mitigations (kv-prefix cache tuning, canary rollback plan, Dedicated pilot), and security/audit asks. Agreed next steps and owners.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: ok hi everyone thanks for joining, we're going to keep this tight 45 minutes, uh follow up from the incident on the 8th. um jonas and i will walk through what we found and proposed mitigations.
[00:08] Priya Singh: yeah thanks Maya, quick note, we have Liam and Elena on because security and platform need clarity, can you confirm the timeline?
[00:14] Maya Patel: sure, timeline first, outage started ~01/08 14:12 UTC, latency spikes across several routes, peak p99 to 14s, errors up 6% for ~22 minutes, then partial mitigation via autoscale and fallback to smaller model.
[00:28] Jonas Reed: to add, the stacktrace points at a kernel fallback path on the GPU runtime when the kv cache faced a sudden high-prefix churn; continuous batching made the latency distribution worse under that pattern. so it's a compound issue: request distribution + kernel selector falling back to safe but slower kernels.
[00:45] Liam O'Connor: when you say kernel fallback, is that Redwood runtime doing a binary switch? could you be more concrete?
[00:51] Jonas Reed: yeah so the runtime has an optimized kernel matched to model arch and seqlen; when we detected memory pressure and high compaction, the allocator signaled and we fell back to a more conservative kernel. that path wasn't as latency-optimized. also batching windows expanded because of uneven request keys.
[01:06] Marco Ruiz: right, we saw a ton of prefix cache misses on our end, lots of different user sessions hitting new prefixes from a recent marketing batch.
[01:13] Priya Singh: hmm that explains it. we had a campaign that created a spike in unique user prompts.
[01:18] Maya Patel: ok so root causes summarized: 1) spike in unique prefixes from customer traffic pattern, 2) batching plus cache churn increased memory/allocator pressure, 3) runtime kernel fallback path has higher latency.
[01:28] Elena Martinez: were there any data exposure concerns during the event?
[01:31] Jonas Reed: no, all requests were processed normally, no logs indicated leakage. persistence and KMS calls remained normal. but we do note in postmortem logs that audit logging suffered brief ingestion lag; not a loss of logs just delayed processing.
[01:44] Priya Singh: good to hear. for mitigation you suggested kv-prefix caching? explain what that would look like.
[01:49] Jonas Reed: yes, two prongs: server-side prefix hotset detection and client-side caching hints. server: runtime will detect high churn and keep a small hotset pinned to faster allocator lanes; client: SDK will expose optional prefix-hint header so spikes from campaigns can be pre-warmed.
[02:06] Liam O'Connor: is that available now or is it a roadmap feature?
[02:09] Jonas Reed: variant: server-side hotset detection is in our next patch, targeted for canary week of 01/18. client prefix-hint SDK change is small but needs release coordination — we can provide a temporary header for your infra to set.
[02:21] Sofia Lopez: (notes) i'll log an SDK ticket and assign to SDK eng if Aurora wants that path.
[02:25] Priya Singh: we probably want both, but timeline matters — can you do server hotset detection fast?
[02:30] Maya Patel: we're prioritizing it. also additional mitigation: we recommended Dedicated capacity pilot to give you reserved capacity and avoid noisy neighbor effects and sudden kernel fallback under shared tenancy burst.
[02:43] Marco Ruiz: Dedicated could help but we need cost estimates.
[02:46] Maya Patel: understood — i'll send a Dedicated pilot proposal and pricing sheet after this call.
[02:51] Elena Martinez: what about the audit logs ingestion lag, that's a compliance risk for us.
[02:55] Jonas Reed: we're adding a durability handoff to persistent logging which ack's to the host earlier; that'll be part of the 01/18 patch. separate item: we can ship an incident log bundle right now for your auditors.
[03:07] Priya Singh: yes please send the bundle.
[03:09] Jonas Reed: noted.
[03:12] Maya Patel: ok on the RCA details — we measured increase in cache miss rate from 4% baseline to 42% during the spike, batching window grew from median 12ms to 210ms under load which amplified p99. the combination triggered fallback.
[03:26] Liam O'Connor: those numbers help. can you share the raw graphs?
[03:29] Jonas Reed: yes i'll attach kernel selector traces, p50/p95/p99, and the allocation heatmaps.
[03:34] Priya Singh: on the mitigation roadmap, can you summarize steps and ETA?
[03:38] Maya Patel: sure — immediate: send incident logs + raw graphs (Jonas) by 01/13; short-term patch: server hotset detection + logging durability fix canary 01/18; SDK hint header release 01/20; Dedicated pilot onboarding start 01/25 (if accepted).
[03:55] Marco Ruiz: if we accept Dedicated pilot, what's rollback if we still see latency spikes?
[03:59] Jonas Reed: we'll do canary routing + model-variant fallback. if tail persists we'll auto-fallback to smaller model variants preserving correctness but lower throughput. and we can throttle or shape the marketing campaign via rate-limiting rules.
[04:13] Elena Martinez: SSO and SOC2 items — we need a checklist of what Redwood provides for audit.
[04:17] Maya Patel: yes, Elena we'll send SOC2 summary, KMS integration docs, RBAC capabilities, and the retention & deletion policy page.
[04:25] Elena Martinez: also need proof of encryption-at-rest for model cache.
[04:29] Jonas Reed: model artifact storage and kv cache metadata are encrypted with customer-specific KMS keys in Dedicated; in hosted we use envelope encryption with customer KMS for Private deployments. i'll include exact config names in the doc.
[04:43] Priya Singh: are there any code-level fixes you need from our side?
[04:47] Jonas Reed: nothing code-level, but if you can mark high-campaign prefixes with the SDK header it helps pre-warm. otherwise server hotset will help us handle it automatically.
[04:56] Liam O'Connor: about benchmarks — could we run a joint controlled test that simulates your marketing spike so we can validate the hotset and Dedicated pilot?
[05:03] Maya Patel: absolutely yes, we recommend a 2-hour window staging test, we'll supply a harness and synthetic traffic template. target date propose 01/26?
[05:12] Priya Singh: 01/26 works for us. what metrics do you want us to collect?
[05:15] Jonas Reed: p50/p95/p99 latency per-route, cache hit ratio, batching window histogram, kernel fallback counts, GPU memory pressure. we'll give you a spreadsheet template.
[05:27] Sofia Lopez: noted; i'll create a shared folder and invite Aurora, we'll put the spreadsheet and the test harness link.
[05:33] Maya Patel: ok circling back to runbook updates — we suggested changes to the on-call playbook: add prefix-churn detection alarms, a play to temporarily disable batching for a route, and clear rollback commands.
[05:45] Priya Singh: disabling batching — is that gradable at route level?
[05:48] Jonas Reed: yes it's per-route runtime config; it's a blunt instrument but effective for immediate p99 relief.
[05:53] Marco Ruiz: we'd need engineering approval to do that during business hours.
[05:56] Maya Patel: understood, we'll put runbook edits into the doc and propose staffing changes.
[05:59] Elena Martinez: one more question on data residency — if we move to Dedicated in eu-west, can logs stay in eu-west?
[06:04] Jonas Reed: yes, regional Dedicated keeps logs & cache in-region; for hosted we can configure log routing to your KMS in-region. we'll confirm exact retention and export capabilities in the SOC2 pack.
[06:16] Priya Singh: ok good.
[06:18] Maya Patel: any other open questions?
[06:20] Liam O'Connor: just the pricing for Dedicated pilot — we'll wait for your sheet.
[06:23] Maya Patel: i'll send pricing and a 30-day pilot SOW draft after call.
[06:27] Sofia Lopez: action items recap: Maya send postmortem + SOW + pricing; Jonas send logs + graphs; Sofia create shared folder; Priya confirm timeline; Elena security checklist.
[06:37] Priya Singh: sounds good, thanks.
[06:39] Maya Patel: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and schedule the test for 01/26. meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings: 'kv' transcribed as 'k V' in one section; 'kernel fallback' is sometimes written as 'kernel fall-back'. timestamps are approximate.
